problem.name: Random circuit sampling
problem.statement_latex: Given an $n$-qubit circuit $U$ with $g$ gates from a specified ensemble, sample $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ from $p_U(x)=|\langle x|U|0^n\rangle|^2$, exactly or within total variation distance $\varepsilon$. Geometry, gate distribution, and noise define the instance family. Complexity uses gates and classical sampling time.
problem.statement_text: Given an $n$-qubit circuit $U$ with $g$ gates from a specified ensemble, sample $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ from $p_U(x)=|\langle x|U|0^n\rangle|^2$, exactly or within total variation distance $\varepsilon$. Geometry, gate distribution, and noise define the instance family. Complexity uses gates and classical sampling time.

strength.description_latex: Ideal sampling compares polynomial quantum cost with the best applicable exponential or subexponential generic classical simulator.
strength.description_text: Ideal sampling compares polynomial quantum cost with the best applicable exponential or subexponential generic classical simulator.

evidence.description_latex: Polynomial approximate classical sampling implies a polynomial-hierarchy collapse under the corresponding average-case hardness and anticoncentration assumptions.
evidence.description_text: Polynomial approximate classical sampling implies a polynomial-hierarchy collapse under the corresponding average-case hardness and anticoncentration assumptions.

hardware.description_latex: Implemented on superconducting processors, including 53-qubit Sycamore; asymptotic comparisons specify target noise and accuracy.
hardware.description_text: Implemented on superconducting processors, including 53-qubit Sycamore; asymptotic comparisons specify target noise and accuracy.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(g+n)$ operations per ideal sample by direct circuit execution and measurement. Finite-gate-set compilation adds its precision overhead.
quantum.headline_text: $O(g+n)$ operations per ideal sample by direct circuit execution and measurement. Finite-gate-set compilation adds its precision overhead.

classical.headline_latex: Use the minimum of state-vector simulation $O(g2^n)$, tensor contraction $\operatorname{poly}(g)2^{O(w)}$ at contraction width $w$, and fixed-algebraic-gate path counting $\operatorname{poly}(s)2^{O(s/\sqrt{\log s})}$ for a sparse Boolean encoding of size $s$ of the required marginal. Sequential conditional probabilities give samples with polynomial overhead. Constant-rate noisy random circuits in the anticoncentration regime admit polynomial-time approximate classical sampling.
classical.headline_text: Use the minimum of state-vector simulation $O(g2^n)$, tensor contraction $\operatorname{poly}(g)2^{O(w)}$ at contraction width $w$, and fixed-algebraic-gate path counting $\operatorname{poly}(s)2^{O(s/\sqrt{\log s})}$ for a sparse Boolean encoding of size $s$ of the required marginal.
